title: autotune: add default batching/caching profiles + quantization profile mappings + unit-econ tooling
author: Alex Johnson
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and caching, introduce quantization profile mappings for common model families, and add unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to expose per-route cost estimates. No breaking changes.
body:
Summary: This PR centralizes and ships a set of production-safe defaults for the Autotune service (batching and prefix/KV caching), introduces a first-pass mapping of quantization profiles for our most used model families, and adds a small UEcon CLI and API endpoint used by ops and product to estimate per-route token unit economics. Motivation: Customers were seeing large variance in cost-per-token and tail latency due to inconsistent batching and cache settings across routes and teams. Autotune previously suggested values but lacked defaults that are safe for new routes and lacked an integrated cost view for engineers. This PR addresses those gaps and enables faster, safer rollouts of autotune recommendations.

Changes (high level): - Autotune service: add default recommendation layer that applies conservative batching/caching defaults when no historical traffic available. Defaults include: batching.max_batch_size=32, batching.max_wait_ms=12, caching.prefix_kv_enabled=true, caching.kv_ttl_secs=300. - Quantization profiles: add profile mappings for gpt2-family, llama-family, and bloom-family linking workload characteristics to recommended quantization (fp16/int8/q4_0). Profiles live under runtime/quant/profiles and are referenced by model metadata. - UEcon tooling: add a lightweight CLI (cmd/uecon) and internal API endpoint (/internal/uecon/estimate) that given route/model/traffic mix returns estimated per-token cost and 95th-percentile latency delta for recommended config changes. - Console integration: add a new per-route "Cost Estimate" card that queries the internal endpoint and shows delta between current config and autotune default. - Tests: unit tests for defaulting logic, integration test for quant profile selection, e2e for UEcon CLI in CI.

Commit summary: - feat(autotune): defaulting layer + config schema (Alex Johnson) - feat(quant): add profile mappings for 3 families (Alex Johnson) - feat(uecon): initial CLI and internal endpoint (Alex Johnson) - docs: update autotune handbook and console screenshots (Morgan Lee) - test: add unit/integration tests and CI job (Priya Patel)

Files changed (representative): - services/autotune/defaults.go: new defaulting layer and unit tests - runtime/quant/profiles/gpt2.json, llama.json, bloom.json: profile definitions - cmd/uecon/main.go: CLI to estimate unit-econ - internal/uecon/handler.go: internal HTTP handler - console/src/components/CostCard.tsx: UI integration - ci/uecon-e2e.yml: new e2e job - docs/autotune.md: documented defaults and migration notes

Why conservative defaults? The goal is to reduce cost variance for new routes without regressing latency SLOs. Defaults were chosen after running batch simulations on representative workloads from benchmark-lab and perf-canary and validated against production shadow traffic for two weeks.

Review conversation (high level): - Priya Patel (reviewer): "Left a few nits and a question about kv_ttl_secs. Can we make ttl configurable per-route?" - Alex Johnson (author): "Agree, made ttl a per-route override in the schema and added an example in docs." - Morgan Lee (reviewer): "Quant profiles look good. Would like a note in docs about fallback behavior if a model is unrecognized." - Alex Johnson: "Added fallback to 'conservative_fp16' in runtime metadata and documented behavior." - Diego Ramirez (approver): "Verified UEcon outputs against sample traffic; approves pending CI." - Priya Patel: "LGTM after tests pass. Approving."

CI and rollout notes: - CI initially failed on the e2e UEcon job due to a flaky dependency; root cause was a test fixture timing assumption. Fixed by adding a retry and increased fixture timeout. - All other checks green: unit tests, lint, staticcheck, integration. - New CI job added to catch UEcon e2e regressions (ci/uecon-e2e.yml).

Backward compatibility and migration: - No breaking API changes. Autotune defaults are additive and only applied when no explicit config exists for a route. Routes with explicit user configs keep current behavior. - Added migration doc with sample snippets to opt-out or override defaults in route config.

Performance and cost impact: - Internal benchmarking shows median cost per token reduced by ~9% for new routes when applying autosuggested defaults, with p95 latency increase < 3ms in most workloads. - Quantization mappings expected to reduce GPU memory and improve throughput for large models when safe quantization is available; profiling is required before enabling aggressively.

Post-merge steps: - Monitor autotune.default_applied metric for unexpected usage spikes. - Run staggered rollout to 10% of new routes for two weeks, then increase. - Follow-up PR planned to add telemetry for quant profile selection and to expose per-model confidence scores (ENG-3825).

Merge: Squash and merge. Branch cleanup done after merge. Contact: alex@redwood.ai for follow-ups.
comments: Priya Patel: Please ensure ttl is overrideable per-route; otherwise LGTM.
Alex Johnson: ttl made configurable per-route; added example to docs.
Morgan Lee: Added fallback behavior for unknown models to conservative_fp16 — looks good.
Diego Ramirez: Verified UEcon estimates on sample traffic; approving.
